summary: Fort Reliance Seaplane Base (YFL) is a remote seaplane facility serving the small settlement of Fort Reliance in Canada's Northwest Territories, situated near the eastern arm of Great Slave Lake. The area has historical significance dating back to the 1930s Yellowknife gold rush, when it served as a base camp for prospectors. Today it primarily supports fly-in fishing lodges, outfitters, and seasonal access to the surrounding wilderness.
faqs:
Q: What aircraft can use Fort Reliance Seaplane Base?
A: The base accommodates float-equipped bush planes, typically single-engine aircraft such as DHC-2 Beavers, DHC-3 Otters, and Cessna 206s on floats.

Q: Are there scheduled flights to YFL?
A: No scheduled commercial service operates to Fort Reliance. Access is primarily through charter bush plane operators based in Yellowknife.

Q: What is the primary purpose of this seaplane base?
A: It serves remote fishing camps, hunting outfitters, and occasional supply runs to the small community of Fort Reliance.

Q: Is there a terminal building at the seaplane base?
A: Facilities are minimal, typical of remote northern seaplane bases. There is no conventional terminal; passengers are met directly on the dock or shore.
transport_tips: There are no roads connecting Fort Reliance to outside communities, so float plane charter from Yellowknife is the only practical way in or out. Book charters well in advance during peak summer fishing season, as bush plane availability can be limited. Travelers should prepare for flexible scheduling, as weather on Great Slave Lake can delay flights unexpectedly.
local_tip: Bring mosquito netting and a head net — the late-June to mid-July window, while prime for fishing, is notoriously buggy near the shoreline, and outfitters often emphasize this in their packing lists.
